newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Pakhoed profits cut by one-off charge.
newsitem.headline: Pakhoed profits cut by one-off charge.

text.p: Dutch tank storage and shipping group Pakhoed NV on Tuesday posted a 1996 net profit from ordinary operations of 138.3 million guilders, up from 123.6 million in 1995, at the high end of market expectations.
Restructuring charges, which were mainly taken in the first half of the year, sliced the 1996 total net profit to 75.5 million guilders, well below from 1995's 121.5 million.

The one-off charges were taken for the reorganisation of Pakhoed's Rotterdam-based units and for the sale of troubled subsidiary Furness, which combined port activities, car dealerships and logistics.
Analysts had expected Pakhoed to produce a 1996 net from ordinary operations of between 125 and 140 million guilders.
The shares by mid-afternoon stood 0.40 guilders higher at 59.70 against the backdrop of a sharply weaker Amsterdam bourse.
The company said it remained positive about profit growth in coming years and expected 1997 net profit to be "substantially" higher than the 1996 figure.
"Pakhoed expects the positive development in profit will continue in 1997. We expect a substantially higher profit," the company said in a statement.

"As chemical manufacturers are concentrating on their core business of manufacturing and marketing, Pakhoed is confident it can capture opportunities to fulfil a key role in logistics and distribution," the company said.
Chemical distribution will fully contribute to the current year's results with the turn-around of the U.S. operations in full swing.
The oil-storage activities in Rotterdam were expected to yield positive operating results because of the restructuring which took place in 1996.
Results of the shipping division were expected to show further growth, the company added.
Pakhoed also took over U.S. chemicals distributor Univar in 1996. The company said it was now market leader in the U.S. in the distribution business and second largest in Europe.
